_README: Hand-authored. Every surface running this brand, and the version it was last synced to. The linter reads syncedVersion and warns when one trails the current release, so 'which of our things are on the old brand' has an answer that is not a guess. Add a row the day a surface is created, not the day it drifts.

consumers.name: The brand portal
consumers.note: Generated from this repository on every push. Cannot drift, which is why its version is recorded as auto rather than as a number somebody has to remember to update.

consumers.name: EVERY1 brand site
consumers.note: Published from every1/ in this repository by the same build as the portal, so the two cannot disagree, and served from its own domain and its own Pages project so EVERY1 stands alone. It carries its own copies of the stylesheet, the faces and its marks: a partner organisation is never sent to the parent's domain, and the site does not go dark if that domain does.

consumers.name: @theword/brand
consumers.note: Version stamped by tools/build_ai.py and checked by L15. Not yet published to a registry: publishing needs an npm account and an organisation scope.

consumers.name: @theword/ui
consumers.note: Components hand-written, version stamped by the build. L15 fails if a specified component is not exported.

consumers.name: THE WORD Branding Kit
consumers.note: The kit to keep. Its colours and fonts still have to be set by hand: Canva's Connect API is read-only for both, so no script can do it. The approved marks are already uploaded and filed (see canva-assets). Run tools/sync_canva.py for the sheet, set the six colours and three families, rename the kit to carry the version, then set syncedVersion here.

consumers.name: THE WORD FOR ALL THE WORLD
consumers.note: The duplicate. Move anything worth keeping out of it and delete it, so there is one answer to what the brand red is. Deleting a kit is not reversible, which is why no script does it.

consumers.name: THE WORD brand library
consumers.note: Not created yet. tools/sync_figma.py pushes variables and styles once a file key and a personal access token exist.

consumers.name: THE WORD · Brand v7.0 (Canva folder)
consumers.syncedBy: tools/sync_canva.py, assets uploaded from the published PNGs
consumers.note: The five approved marks, uploaded from their public URLs on brand.theword.world so the files in Canva are the published files rather than someone's copy. Horizontal and stacked in both inks, plus the glyph for avatars.
